claim.claim-text: 1. . A method (1900) for operating a projector system (300), where the method is implemented by a projector controller (135), the method comprising:

2. . The method (1900) of claim 1, wherein the first translucent display (105) and the second translucent display each include a display face (110) and a projection face (115), wherein the projection face (115) is an opposite side of the respective translucent display (105) from the display face (110); and wherein the first projector (125) projects the first projection sequence on the projection face (115) of the first translucent display (105), and the second projector (125) projects the second projection sequence on the projection face (115) of the second translucent display (105).

3. . The method (1900) of claim 2, wherein the first projector (125) projects the first projection sequence on the projection face (115) of the first translucent display (105) in reverse such that the first projection sequence is displayed in proper orientation on the display face (110) of the first translucent display, and the second projector (125) projects the second projection sequence on the projection face (115) of the second translucent display (105) in reverse such that the second projection sequence is displayed in proper orientation on the display face (110) of the second translucent display.

4. . The method (1900) of any preceding claim, wherein the first translucent display is configured as a countertop (405), sink area (410), splash back area (415), wall (705, 1205), ceiling, floor (1210), toilet (1220), toilet lid (1225), toilet seat (1230), toilet shroud (1235), cabinet face, passenger seat, tray table, or bar unit.

5. . The method (1900) of any preceding claim, wherein the second translucent display is configured as a countertop (405), sink area (410), splash back area (415), wall (705, 1205), ceiling, floor (1210), toilet (1220), toilet lid (1225), toilet seat (1230), toilet shroud (1235), cabinet face, passenger seat, or bar unit.

6. . The method (1900) of any preceding claim, wherein the first sensor (305) includes a door lock sensor, a flush sensor, a faucet sensor, a motion sensor, a thermal sensor, or an automatic paper towel dispenser sensor.

7. . The method (1900) of any preceding claim, wherein the second sensor (305) includes a door lock sensor, a flush sensor, a faucet sensor, a motion sensor, a thermal sensor, or an automatic paper towel dispenser sensor.
8. . The method (1900) of any preceding claim, further comprising:

9. . The method (1900) of claim 8, wherein the third translucent display (105) includes a display face (110) and a projection face (115), wherein the projection face (115) is an opposite side of the third translucent display (105) from the display face (110); and wherein the third projector (125) projects the third projection sequence on the projection face (115) of the third translucent display (105).

10. . The method (1900) of claim 9, wherein the third projector (125) projects the third projection sequence on the projection face (115) of the third translucent display (105) in reverse such that the third projection sequence is displayed in proper orientation on the display face (110) of the third translucent display.

11. . The method (1900) of any preceding claim, wherein the third translucent display is configured as a countertop (405), sink area (410), splash back area (415), wall (705, 1205), ceiling, floor (1210), toilet (1220), toilet lid (1225), toilet seat (1230), toilet shroud (1235), cabinet face, passenger seat, tray table, or bar unit.

12. . The method (1900) of any preceding claim, wherein the third sensor (305) includes a door lock sensor, a flush sensor, a faucet sensor, a motion sensor, a thermal sensor, or an automatic paper towel dispenser sensor.
13. . The method of any of claims 8-12, further comprising:
14. . A system (300) comprising:
15. . A vehicle comprising the system of claim 14, optionally wherein the vehicle is an aircraft.
